title: Jaipur
selection: Rajasthan recorded 2.07 million foreign tourist visits in 2024, fifth among states (India Tourism Data Compendium 2025, Table 4.1.2). Jaipur is the state capital and the third point of the Delhi–Agra–Jaipur Golden Triangle; it holds two UNESCO World Heritage Sites (Jantar Mantar and Amber Fort, part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan) and the walled city is itself a World Heritage City.

JP1.topic: Founded in 1727 by Jai Singh II
JP1.claim: Jaipur was founded in 1727 by the Kachhwaha Rajput ruler Jai Singh II, who named it after himself; it is believed to be India's first planned city of the Common Era.

evidence.quote: It was established in 1727 by Kachhwaha Rajput ruler Jai Singh II, who named it after himself.

JP2.topic: Why the Pink City is pink
JP2.claim: The city was painted pink in 1876 to welcome the Prince of Wales, giving Jaipur its name 'Pink City'.

evidence.quote: the city was painted pink to welcome Albert Edward, Prince of Wales in 1876
In 1876, to welcome the Prince of Wales, Maharaja Ram Singh of Jaipur had the entire city painted pink, as the colour symbolised hospitality.

JP3.claim: Jaipur was named to UNESCO's World Heritage list as a city on 6 July 2019.

evidence.quote: On 6 July 2019, the city was named to the World Heritage Cities list.

JP4.claim: Jaipur is one of the three points of the Golden Triangle with Delhi and Agra.

evidence.quote: is one of the three points of the Golden Triangle, which comprises Delhi, Agra, and Jaipur

JP5.claim: Jaipur is about 268 km from New Delhi and 232 km from Agra by road; the Ministry of Tourism puts the drive from Delhi at about 5 hours.

evidence.quote: Located 268 km (167 miles) from the national capital New Delhi
Jaipur - 232 km
It is 5 hours from Delhi via the well-maintained NH 8

JP6.claim: Jaipur has direct trains to major cities, including the Shatabdi and Rajdhani to Delhi.

evidence.quote: Jaipur Railway Station offers direct trains to major cities, including Delhi via Shatabdi, Rajdhani, Duronto, and Mandor Express.

JP7.claim: Jaipur International Airport is at Sanganer, about 10 km south of the city centre.

evidence.quote: It is located in the southern suburb of Sanganer , located about 10 km (6.2 mi) from the city centre.

JP8.claim: The Jaipur Metro's Pink Line runs east–west between Mansarovar and Badi Chaupar in the old city.

evidence.quote: Phase 1 of the Jaipur Metro project comprises the East–West Corridor between Mansarovar and Badi Chaupar

JP9.claim: Jaipur has long, extremely hot summers and short, mild winters; most rain falls in July and August.

evidence.quote: with long, extremely hot summers and short mild to warm winters
falling mostly in July and August due to the southwest monsoon

JP10.claim: Must-try dishes include dal baati churma, kachori, mirchi bada, ker sangri and, for non-vegetarians, laal maas.

evidence.quote: Some of the must-try dishes in Jaipur include the iconic Dal Bati Churma
Non-vegetarians can head for Laal Maas, a signature Rajasthani dish

JP11.claim: Masala Chowk, at Ram Niwas Bagh, gathers Jaipur's street food in one place.

evidence.quote: a place where you get to celebrate and indulge in the tastes of the street food of Jaipur

JP12.claim: Johari Bazaar is known for jewellery and textiles and Bapu Bazaar for mojari shoes and textiles; the markets are generally closed on Sundays.

evidence.quote: Johari Bazaar Road is famous for Rajasthani jewellery, clothing, and textiles. Bapu Bazar is known for Mojari, camel skin shoes, and Rajasthani textiles.

JP13.claim: Jaipur is known for block-printed textiles — Sanganeri, Bagru and Dabu prints.

evidence.quote: Jaipur is famous for its block print textiles, known for Sanganeri prints, Bagru prints, and Dabu prints.

JP14.claim: Jaipur's festivals include Gangaur, the Jaipur Literature Festival, the Kite Festival and Teej.

evidence.quote: including the Gangaur Festival, Jaipur Literature Festival, Kite Festival, Teej Festival

JP15.claim: The Incredible India tourist infoline is 1800-11-1363; 112 is India's single emergency number.

evidence.quote: Incredible India Tourist Infoline 1800-11-1363
112 is now the pan-country single emergency number for all emergencies.

JP16.claim: e-Tourist visa applications should be made at least 4 days before arrival, with a passport valid for at least six months.

evidence.quote: For e-Tourist and e-Business visa, Applicants of the eligible countries/territories may apply online minimum 4 days in advance of the date of arrival.

evidence.quote: The UPI One World wallet can be availed through authorized PPI issuers at airports, hotels, designated money exchange locations and other touchpoints, following a full KYC process based on a passport and valid visa.

evidence.quote: the Amer Fort was commissioned by Maharaja Man Singh I in 1592

evidence.quote: in 2013, Amer Fort, along with five other forts of Rajasthan, was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the group Hill Forts of Rajasthan

AM6.claim: Underground tunnels link Amber Fort to Jaigarh Fort on the hill above; some sections have been restored.

evidence.quote: sweeping views of Maota Lake below make it a must-visit destination

HM1.claim: Hawa Mahal was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh and designed by Lal Chand Ustad.

evidence.quote: Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, the grandson of Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh and designed by Lal Chand Ustad

evidence.quote: Hawa Mahal derives its name from its 953 windows, known as jharokhas , which are arranged in a honeycomb-like pattern.

HM3.claim: There is no front entrance — visitors enter from the rear and climb ramps rather than stairs.

evidence.quote: there is no front entrance, only a rear one. Instead of stairs, there are ramps to the upper floors

HM4.claim: Hawa Mahal is open from 9 am to 4:30 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 09:00 AM Closing time - 04:30 PM

HM5.claim: Inside is a museum of Rajasthani miniature art.

evidence.quote: Inside is a museum that houses Rajasthani miniature art

CP1.claim: The City Palace was founded by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in 1727 as part of his new city, and blends Rajput and Mughal architecture.

evidence.quote: this beautiful palace was founded in 1727 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II as part of his ambitious city project

CP2.claim: The palace houses the Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II Museum and is still home to Jaipur's royal family.

evidence.quote: It now houses the Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II Museum, and continues to be the home of the Jaipur royal family.

CP3.claim: The Mubarak Mahal in the first courtyard holds part of the museum; the seven-storey Chandra Mahal towers over the complex.

evidence.quote: This exquisite building houses part of the Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II Museum today.
a seven-level architectural marvel

CP4.claim: A standard ticket covers the first floor of the Chandra Mahal; a separate 'Royal Splendour' ticket opens the upper, private floors.

evidence.quote: While a standard ticket allows access to the first floor, the 'Royal Splendour' ticket allows access to other exclusive areas.

CP5.claim: The City Palace is open from 9:30 am to 7:30 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 9.30 AM Closing time - 7.30 PM

CP6.claim: The palace is in the heart of the old city, about 4 km from the railway station.

evidence.quote: this palace is nestled just four kilometres from the railway station in the heart of Jaipur

evidence.quote: The Jantar Mantar is a collection of 19 astronomy instruments constructed between 1728 – 1734 AD.

JM2.claim: Jai Singh II built five observatories across India; Jaipur's is the largest.

evidence.quote: It features the world's largest stone sundial , and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site .

evidence.quote: is 88 feet (27 m) high, making it one of the world's largest sundials
a colossal sundial that measures time with an astonishing accuracy of 2 seconds

JM5.claim: Jantar Mantar is open from 9 am to 5 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 09:00 AM Closing time - 05:00 PM

JM6.topic: Next to City Palace and Hawa Mahal
JM6.claim: Jantar Mantar is next to the City Palace and a short drive from Hawa Mahal.

evidence.quote: It is near City Palace and Hawa Mahal .

evidence.quote: It was constructed during the reign of Jai Singh in 1734, and was later expanded in 1868.

NG2.topic: Views over Jaipur and Jal Mahal
NG2.claim: Nahargarh has panoramic views over Jaipur and the Jal Mahal, which is itself no longer open to tourists.

evidence.quote: it provides panoramic views of Jaipur as well as the Jal Mahal, which is no longer open to tourists

NG3.claim: The fort houses a Sculpture Park set up by the Government of Rajasthan.

evidence.quote: the Fort also houses the Sculpture Park

JG1.claim: Jaigarh Fort was commissioned in 1726 by Jai Singh II as the defensive bastion for the Amber Fort complex below it.

evidence.quote: Jaigarh Fort, commissioned in 1726 by the Rajput ruler Jai Singh II
this imposing fortress was built to be the frontier defence bastion for the grand Amber Fort and palace complex in its shadow
known as the Cheelka Teela, or the "Hill of Eagles,"

JG2.claim: The fort displays the Jaivana cannon, which the Ministry of Tourism describes as the largest cannon on wheels.

evidence.quote: remains the largest cannon on wheels to this day

JG3.claim: Jaigarh Fort is open from 9:30 am to 5 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 09:30 AM Closing time - 05:00 PM

NG4.claim: Inside Nahargarh, the Madhvendra Palace was built by Sawai Ram Singh for his nine queens.

evidence.quote: MADHVENDRA PALACE, NAHARGARH
the Madhvendra Palace was built by Sawai Ram Singh for his nine queens.

NG5.claim: The Jaipur Wax Museum is inside Nahargarh Fort.

evidence.quote: Amidst the confines of the Nahargarh Fort at the foothills of the Aravallis lies the Jaipur wax museum

JG4.claim: Visitors enter through the triple-arched Awani Darwaza; inside are the Lalit Mandir, Vilas Mandir and Laxmi Vilas palaces.

evidence.quote: Step through the majestic Awani Darwaza, a triple-arched entrance
The stately Lalit Mandir, the regal Vilas Mandir, and the serene Laxmi Vilas

JG5.claim: In the Mughal era Jaigarh became the dynasty's main cannon foundry.

evidence.quote: it became the primary cannon foundry for the dynasty

AH1.claim: Commissioned in 1868 to designs by Samuel Swinton Jacob, the Albert Hall Museum opened to the public in 1887.

evidence.quote: In 1868, Maharaja Sawai Ram Singh II commissioned this magnificent edifice, which was brought to life through the masterful design of Samuel Swinton Jacob.
Maharaja Sawai Madho Singh II opened the museum to the public in 1887.

AH2.claim: Its 16 galleries display about 20,000 artefacts, including miniature paintings, arms, a Persian garden carpet and an Egyptian mummy.

evidence.quote: Prepare to be enchanted by the museum's 16 galleries
the sheer diversity of the 20,000 artefacts on display
Notable treasures inside the museum include the rare Persian Garden Carpet and an Egyptian mummy.

AH3.claim: Incredible India lists the museum's hours as 9 am–5 pm and 7–9:30 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 09.00 AM - 05:00 PM and 07:00 PM - 09.30 PM

AH4.claim: The museum stands in Ram Niwas Garden, laid out in 1868, which also has a bird park, a zoo and an art gallery.

evidence.quote: This historical garden was built by Maharaja Sawai Ram Singh in 1868.
the garden houses the Albert Hall Museum (now known as Central Museum), a bird park, a zoo, the Ravindra Rang Manch theatre, an art gallery and an exhibition ground.

AH5.claim: The building is lit up in colour every night.

evidence.quote: Every night, the museum comes alive in a mesmerising display of vibrant, colourful lights

JL1.claim: Jal Mahal stands in Man Sagar Lake; most of the building is under water, with only the top floor showing.

evidence.quote: Welcome to Jal Mahal, a majestic palace rising from the still waters of Man Sagar Lake.
most of the building rests submerged beneath the lake's surface, with only the top floor visible.

JL2.claim: Its foundations date from 1699; when the lake is full, the lower four of its five storeys are under water.

evidence.quote: Back in 1699, the foundation of this magnificent palace was laid
the lower 4 storeys remain submerged underwater

JL3.claim: The palace is seen from the roadside promenade on the lake's west side, and is lit up at night.

evidence.quote: The Man Sagar Dam faces eastward while the local roadside promenade faces west.

GT1.claim: Galtaji is a Hindu pilgrimage site in the Aravalli Hills about 10 km east of Jaipur.

evidence.quote: Galtaji is situated in the Aravalli Hills, about 10 km east of Jaipur, Rajasthan.

GT2.claim: The pink-sandstone complex has temples, pavilions and seven holy kunds fed by springs; its monkeys give it the nickname Monkey Temple.

evidence.quote: It's not just a temple but a vast complex housing numerous pavilions, holy 'kunds' (water tanks), shrines, and natural springs
One of the most fascinating features of the Galta Ji Temple is its seven holy 'kunds' or water tanks
These cheeky residents are the reason behind the whimsical nickname of this sanctuary—the Monkey Temple.

GT3.claim: Galtaji draws its biggest crowds at Makar Sankranti in January.

evidence.quote: This is when the temple attracts a significant crowd during the Makar Sankranti festival.

BM1.claim: The white-marble Lakshmi Narayan (Birla) temple, built by the Birla family in 1988, stands at the foot of Moti Dungri.

evidence.quote: The Lakshmi-Narayan Temple, or the Birla Temple, as it is more popularly known as, is located at the base of Moti Dungari.
It was built in 1988 by the illustrious Birla family

BM2.claim: Incredible India lists the temple's hours as 8 am–noon and 4–8 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 08:00 AM - 12:00 PM and 04:00 PM - 08:00 PM

BM3.claim: Inside are images of Vishnu and Lakshmi carved from a single marble slab, stained-glass windows and a small Birla family museum.

evidence.quote: The intricate carvings of Lord Vishnu and Goddess Lakshmi sculpted from a single marble slab are exceptionally breathtaking.
A museum showcasing the Birla Family's most cherished possessions is tucked away within the temple's sacred halls.

GD1.claim: Govind Dev Ji, in the City Palace grounds, is a spire-less temple housing the Krishna idol that Sawai Jai Singh II brought from Vrindavan.

evidence.quote: Nestled within the glorious confines of Jaipur's iconic City Palace
The Krishna temple is a rare spire-less temple and houses the idol of Govind Devji that Sawai Jai Singh brought from Vrindavan.

GD2.claim: It is busiest at Janmashtami and Holi; its prayer hall holds a Guinness record for the widest single-span RCC flat roof.

evidence.quote: You should consider visiting during the festivals of Janmashtami and Holi when the temple is thronged by thousands of devotees
which has the widest single-span RCC flat roof

GD3.claim: A 3-D projection-mapped light and sound show at Jainiwas Udyan tells the temple's story.

evidence.quote: Light & Sound Show at Jainiwas Udhyan is one of the first 3-D projection mapping-based light & sound show in Rajasthan
Show depicts story of world-famous Shri Govind Dev Ji temple of Jaipur

MD1.claim: The Moti Dungri Ganesh temple, built in 1761, is about 6 km from Jaipur Junction station and is the city's most important Ganesh temple.

evidence.quote: Situated a mere 6 kilometres from the Jaipur Junction Railway Station
Constructed in 1761 by the visionary Seth Jai Ram Paliwal
Visitors go there to pay homage at the famous Ganesh temple, the most auspicious and important religious temple in Jaipur.

GG1.claim: Garh Ganesh sits on an Aravalli hilltop reached by about 365 steps, with wide views over Jaipur.

evidence.quote: To reach the temple, you need to climb around 365 steps, representing the number of days in a year.
the temple also offers striking panoramic views of Jaipur city.

GG2.claim: Incredible India lists the temple's hours as 7:30 am–noon and 4–8:30 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 07:30 AM - 12:00 PM and 04:00 PM - 08:30 PM

PK1.claim: Panna Meena ka Kund is a centuries-old stepwell in Amer, once a water source and meeting place for the neighbourhood.

evidence.quote: the Jaipur Stepwell, or Panna Meena Ka Kund, is a popular attraction, which is again, located in Amer.
Residents would congregate in the stepwell to exchange stories, get water, and escape the oppressive desert sun

GA1.claim: Gaitore, just off the Jaipur–Amer road, holds the marble and sandstone chhatris of Jaipur's rulers, cremated here from 1733.

evidence.quote: Just off the Jaipur-Amber road is Gaitore, where the former Maharajas of Jaipur are entombed.
meticulously crafted from marble and sandstone
From 1733 onwards, each Kachhwaha ruler was honoured with a final rite of passage at this hallowed ground

AN1.claim: The Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing, in a restored haveli a ten-minute walk through Amer's old streets, opened in 2005 and shows block-printed textiles and tools.

evidence.quote: At a mere ten-minute walk through the cobbled streets of Amber lies the Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing.
Opened in 2005, the museum is an initiative of the founders of Anokhi
Located in a magnificently restored haveli (mansion), the museum displays a varied selection of block-printed textiles alongside images, tools and related objects

AN2.claim: The restored haveli received a UNESCO heritage conservation award in 2000.

evidence.quote: Cultural Heritage Conservation Award in 2000

JB1.claim: Johari Bazaar is known for jewellery, clothes and textiles; Rajasthali, the government showroom on MI Road, and Nehru, Bapu and Tripolia bazaars are the other main shopping streets.

evidence.quote: Johari Bazaar Road is famous for Rajasthani jewellery, clothing, and textiles.
The famous shopping spots are Rajasthali (the Rajasthan Government showroom on MI Road), Johari Bazaar, MI road, Nehru Bazaar, Bapu Bazaar, and stalls at Bari and Choti Chaupurs.

JB2.claim: Lac bangles, made by Jaipur artisans, are a classic buy.

evidence.quote: Skilfully crafted by artisans in Jaipur using lac, a resinous substance derived from the secretions of the lac insect

IS1.claim: Isarlat (Swarg Suli) is a 60-ft minaret near Tripolia Gate, built by Raja Ishwari Singh in 1749 to mark a victory, with views over the city.

this tower near Tripolia Gate was built by Raja Ishwari Singh in 1749 A.D to commemorate a grand victory.
Ishwar Lat offers a breath-taking view of Jaipur.

SR1.claim: Sisodia Rani Palace and Garden, 8 km out on the Agra road, is a terraced Mughal-style garden with fountains and murals of Radha and Krishna.

places.name: Jaipur
places.summary: Rajasthan's Pink City: Amber Fort, Hawa Mahal, the City Palace and Jantar Mantar, bazaars full of block prints and gems — the third point of the Golden Triangle.
places.seoTitle: Jaipur Travel Guide: Amber Fort, Hawa Mahal & City Palace
places.seoDescription: Plan your Jaipur trip: Amber Fort, Hawa Mahal, City Palace and Jantar Mantar timings, getting there from Delhi and Agra, bazaars, food and a 2-day itinerary.

images.alt: The pink, honeycomb facade of Hawa Mahal with its hundreds of small windows in Jaipur
images.caption: Hawa Mahal, Jaipur

overview.text:
Jaipur was founded in 1727 by Jai Singh II, who named it after himself, and was laid out as one of India's earliest planned cities. Its old city earned the name 'Pink City' in 1876, when it was painted pink to welcome the Prince of Wales, and in 2019 the walled city was added to UNESCO's World Heritage list.

The capital of Rajasthan, Jaipur is the third point of the Golden Triangle with Delhi and Agra. Its sights fall into two groups. In the old city, Hawa Mahal, the City Palace and the Jantar Mantar observatory — another World Heritage Site — are within a few minutes of each other. About 11 km north, Amber Fort and Jaigarh Fort crown the hills above Maota Lake, with Nahargarh on the ridge in between.

Two days covers the essentials: one for Amber and the hill forts, one for the old city and its bazaars. Note that the markets generally close on Sundays.

items.body: Amber Fort: the 16th-century hill palace with its mirror-covered Sheesh Mahal.
Hawa Mahal: 953 latticed windows on a five-storey facade, built in 1799.
City Palace: still home to Jaipur's royal family, with a museum of royal collections.
Jantar Mantar: 18th-century astronomical instruments, including the world's largest stone sundial.
Nahargarh at sunset: the whole city spread out below the ridge.

best_time.text: Jaipur has long, extremely hot summers and short, mild winters, so the cooler months are by far the most comfortable for climbing forts and walking the bazaars. Most rain falls in July and August. The city's festival calendar is a good reason to time a visit: the Jaipur Literature Festival, the Kite Festival, Gangaur and Teej all draw crowds.

how_to_reach.text:
By road, Jaipur is about 268 km from New Delhi — the Ministry of Tourism puts the drive at about 5 hours — and 232 km from Agra, which makes it the natural last stop of a Golden Triangle trip. Direct trains, including the Shatabdi and Rajdhani, link Jaipur station with Delhi; book on IRCTC.

Jaipur International Airport is at Sanganer, about 10 km south of the centre.

local_transport.text: The Jaipur Metro's Pink Line runs east–west from Mansarovar to Badi Chaupar in the old city, useful for reaching the bazaar area. For Amber, Jaigarh and Nahargarh in the hills, hire a taxi or auto-rickshaw for the half day — agree the fare and waiting time in advance.

where_to_stay.text: Staying in or near the walled old city puts Hawa Mahal, the City Palace and the bazaars within walking distance, though streets are busy and noisy. Quieter areas with more space lie outside the walls to the south and west. Amber is a short drive north whichever you choose.

overview.text:
Amber — also spelt Amer — sits on a hill about 11 km from central Jaipur, looking down over Maota Lake. Raja Man Singh I began the palace in 1592, and it was the seat of the Kachhwaha rulers until they moved their capital down to the plains and founded Jaipur. In 2013 it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site as one of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan.

The visit climbs through the Suraj Pol gate into Jaleb Chowk, the old parade ground, then on to the Diwan-e-Aam, the hall of public audience. The highlight is the Sheesh Mahal, a palace of mirrors whose walls and ceilings are covered in tiny pieces of glass. Underground tunnels, partly restored, link Amber with Jaigarh Fort on the hill above. In the evening the fort hosts a sound and light show.

overview.text:
Hawa Mahal, the 'Palace of Winds', was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh and designed by Lal Chand Ustad. Its five-storey facade on the main street of the old city is a honeycomb of 953 small latticed windows, or jharokhas. They were designed so that the royal women, who lived in purdah, could watch everyday life and festival processions in the street below without being seen.

There is no front entrance: you go in from the back and climb ramps, not stairs, to the upper floors for the view through the windows. A small museum inside displays Rajasthani miniature art. The best view of the facade itself is from across the street.

overview.text:
Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II founded the City Palace in 1727 as part of his new city of Jaipur. Its courtyards, halls and gardens mix Rajput and Mughal architecture, and the palace is still home to Jaipur's royal family while also housing the Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II Museum.

You enter through the Virendra Pol into the first courtyard, where the Mubarak Mahal holds part of the museum. Beyond it rises the seven-storey Chandra Mahal. A standard ticket covers its first floor; a separate 'Royal Splendour' ticket opens the private upper floors, including the blue Sukh Niwas. The palace is in the heart of the old city, about 4 km from the railway station.

overview.text:
Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, a keen astronomer, built five observatories across India; Jaipur's, completed between 1728 and 1734, is the largest. It is a collection of 19 instruments in stone and marble for observing the positions of the sun and stars with the naked eye, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The star is the Vrihat Samrat Yantra, a 27 m sundial — the largest stone sundial in the world — whose shadow tells the time to about 2 seconds. A guide makes a big difference here: the instruments only come alive when someone explains how to read them. Jantar Mantar is right next to the City Palace and close to Hawa Mahal.

overview.text:
Nahargarh — the name means 'abode of tigers' — was built in 1734 on the Aravalli ridge that forms the northern backdrop of Jaipur, and expanded in 1868. Once part of the city's defences, today it is best known for its views: the whole of Jaipur spreads out below, with the Jal Mahal in Man Sagar Lake (which is no longer open to visitors) in the distance.

Inside the fort, the Government of Rajasthan has set up a Sculpture Park in the old palace rooms. Come in the late afternoon and stay for sunset over the city.

overview.text:
Jaigarh Fort was commissioned in 1726 by Jai Singh II as the defensive bastion for the Amber palace complex below it, on the hill the Ministry of Tourism calls the 'Hill of Eagles'. Its long walls are visible from everywhere in Amber, and it is linked to Amber Fort by underground tunnels.

The main draw is the Jaivana cannon, which the Ministry of Tourism describes as the largest cannon on wheels. From the ramparts there are views over Amber Fort and Maota Lake.

overview.text:
The Albert Hall Museum stands in the middle of Ram Niwas Garden. Maharaja Sawai Ram Singh II commissioned it in 1868 to designs by Samuel Swinton Jacob, and Maharaja Sawai Madho Singh II opened it to the public in 1887.

Its 16 galleries hold about 20,000 artefacts — miniature paintings, sculpture, textiles, arms, jewellery, a rare Persian garden carpet and an Egyptian mummy. After dark the building is lit up in colour.

items.body: 9 am – 5 pm and 7 – 9:30 pm (Incredible India)

items.title: Where
items.body: Ram Niwas Garden, which also has a bird park, a zoo and an art gallery
Come back after 7 pm to see the building lit up.
Eat Jaipur street food at Masala Chowk in Ram Niwas Bagh.
Continue to the white-marble Birla Mandir below Moti Dungri.

places.name: Jal Mahal
places.summary: The 'Water Palace' rising from Man Sagar Lake on the road to Amber — seen from the lakeside promenade.
places.seoTitle: Jal Mahal Jaipur: The Water Palace on Man Sagar Lake
places.seoDescription: Jal Mahal, Jaipur's Water Palace in Man Sagar Lake: its history from 1699, why four of its five storeys are under water, and where to see it.

images.commons: File:Man Sagar Lake with Jal Mahal Palace, Jaipur, 20191218 1427 9225.jpg
images.alt: Jal Mahal in the middle of Man Sagar Lake
images.caption: Jal Mahal

overview.text:
Jal Mahal rises from Man Sagar Lake beside the road from Jaipur to Amber. Its foundations date from 1699; when the lake is full, the lower four of its five storeys are under water, so only the top floor shows.

The palace itself is not open to tourists. You see it from the roadside promenade on the lake's west shore, and it is lit up at night. Nearby, the royal cenotaphs at Gaitore make a quiet stop.

items.body: Stop on the way to or from Amber Fort — it is on the same road.
Come at sunset or after dark, when the palace is lit.
For the view from above, go up to Nahargarh Fort.

items.title: Entry
items.body: The palace is not open to visitors; it is seen from the promenade on the west shore

items.title: Best view from above
items.body: Nahargarh Fort, on the ridge over the city

places.name: Galtaji
places.summary: A spring-fed temple complex in the Aravalli hills east of Jaipur, known as the Monkey Temple.
places.seoTitle: Galtaji Temple Jaipur: The Monkey Temple & Holy Kunds
places.seoDescription: Galtaji, about 10 km east of Jaipur: a pink-sandstone temple complex with seven spring-fed kunds in the Aravalli hills, busiest at Makar Sankranti.

images.commons: File:Zanana Kund Aur Galta Ji Ka Mandir - edited.jpg
images.alt: Galtaji temple and its kund in the Aravalli hills
images.caption: Galtaji

overview.text:
Galtaji is a Hindu pilgrimage site tucked into the Aravalli hills about 10 km east of Jaipur. More palace than temple in looks, the pink-sandstone complex has temples, pavilions and seven holy kunds (water tanks) fed by natural springs.

Troops of monkeys live around the complex — hence its nickname, the Monkey Temple.

items.body: Seven holy kunds, fed by water flowing from the Gaumukh, a rock shaped like a cow's head.
The Galta Kund, the most revered of them.
The spot where Tulsidas is said to have written part of the Ramcharitmanas.

how_to_reach.text: Galtaji is about 10 km east of Jaipur in the Aravalli hills; go by rickshaw, cab or car.

best_time.text: It is busiest at Makar Sankranti in January, when pilgrims come to bathe; Jaipur's cooler months make the climb easier.

items.body: Keep food out of sight — the monkeys are bold.
Dress modestly; this is an active pilgrimage site.

places.name: Birla Mandir
places.summary: A white-marble Lakshmi Narayan temple at the foot of Moti Dungri, built in 1988.
places.seoTitle: Birla Mandir Jaipur: Timings & What to See
places.seoDescription: Birla Mandir (Lakshmi Narayan Temple), Jaipur: a 1988 white-marble temple below Moti Dungri, with carved images, stained glass and evening lighting.

images.alt: The white-marble Birla Mandir in Jaipur
images.caption: Birla Mandir

overview.text: The Lakshmi Narayan temple — better known as Birla Mandir — was built of white marble by the Birla family in 1988 and stands at the foot of Moti Dungri. Inside are images of Vishnu and Lakshmi carved from a single marble slab, stained-glass windows showing stories of the gods, and a small museum of the Birla family's possessions.

items.title: Hours
items.body: 8 am – noon and 4 – 8 pm (Incredible India)
Visit the Moti Dungri Ganesh temple next door.
Combine with the Albert Hall Museum.

best_time.text: Come in the evening, when the temple reopens at 4 pm and its three marble domes are lit up after dark.

how_to_reach.text: It stands at the foot of Moti Dungri, next to the Ganesh temple, about 6 km from Jaipur Junction station.

places.name: Govind Dev Ji Temple
places.summary: The Jaipur royal family's Krishna temple, in the City Palace grounds.
places.seoTitle: Govind Dev Ji Temple Jaipur: History & Festivals
places.seoDescription: Govind Dev Ji Temple in Jaipur's City Palace grounds: the Krishna idol brought from Vrindavan, the record-breaking prayer hall, and Janmashtami crowds.

images.alt: Devotees at the Govind Dev Ji temple, Jaipur
images.caption: Govind Dev Ji Temple

overview.text: Govind Dev Ji stands within the City Palace grounds. It is a rare spire-less temple, and it houses the image of Krishna that Sawai Jai Singh II brought from Vrindavan; the royal family worshipped it as their own deity, and it remains one of Jaipur's most loved temples. Its prayer hall holds a Guinness record for the widest single-span RCC flat roof.

best_time.text: Janmashtami and Holi draw thousands of devotees. In the evening, a 3-D projection-mapped light and sound show at Jainiwas Udyan tells the temple's story.

items.body: Walk on into the City Palace.
Visit Jantar Mantar next door.

items.title: The idol
items.body: Hidden at Amer in Aurangzeb's reign, brought to Jaipur by Sawai Jai Singh II after 1714

items.title: Where
items.body: In the City Palace grounds, in the old city about 4 km from the railway station

places.name: Moti Dungri Ganesh Temple
places.summary: Jaipur's most important Ganesh temple, built in 1761 at the foot of Moti Dungri hill.
places.seoTitle: Moti Dungri Ganesh Temple Jaipur: History & Location
places.seoDescription: Moti Dungri Ganesh Temple, Jaipur: built in 1761 below Moti Dungri hill, about 6 km from Jaipur Junction, next to the white-marble Birla Mandir.

images.commons: File:Moti Dungri Ganesh Ji Mandir, Jaipur; January 2024.jpg
images.alt: The Moti Dungri Ganesh temple in Jaipur
images.caption: Moti Dungri Ganesh Temple

overview.text: At the foot of Moti Dungri hill, the Ganesh temple built in 1761 by Seth Jai Ram Paliwal is the most important Ganesh temple in the city.

how_to_reach.text: It is about 6 km from Jaipur Junction railway station; the white-marble Birla Mandir stands next to it.

places.name: Garh Ganesh Temple
places.summary: A hilltop Ganesh temple above Jaipur reached by about 365 steps.
places.seoTitle: Garh Ganesh Temple Jaipur: Steps, Views & Timings
places.seoDescription: Garh Ganesh Temple: a hilltop Ganesh shrine above Jaipur, about 365 steps up, with panoramic views over the city; open mornings and evenings.

images.commons: File:Staircase leading to Garh Ganesh Temple, Jaipur.jpg
images.alt: The stairway climbing to Garh Ganesh temple
images.caption: Garh Ganesh Temple

overview.text: Garh Ganesh sits on an Aravalli hilltop above the city. About 365 steps — one for each day of the year — lead up to it, and the climb is rewarded with panoramic views over Jaipur.

items.title: Hours
items.body: 7:30 am – noon and 4 – 8:30 pm (Incredible India)

places.name: Panna Meena ka Kund
places.summary: A geometric old stepwell in Amer town, close to Amber Fort.
places.seoTitle: Panna Meena ka Kund: Jaipur's Stepwell in Amer
places.seoDescription: Panna Meena ka Kund, the stepwell in Amer near Amber Fort: once a water source and meeting place, now one of Jaipur's most photographed spots.

images.commons: File:20191219 Panna Meena ka Kund step well, Amber, Jaipur, 1130 9630.jpg
images.alt: Criss-crossing steps of Panna Meena ka Kund
images.caption: Panna Meena ka Kund

overview.text: Panna Meena ka Kund is a centuries-old stepwell in Amer town, a short walk from Amber Fort. It was once the neighbourhood's water source and a place where people gathered to talk and escape the desert heat; today it is one of Jaipur's most photographed sights.

places.name: Gaitore
places.summary: The marble cenotaphs of Jaipur's rulers, below Nahargarh off the Amber road.
places.seoTitle: Gaitore Ki Chhatriyan: Royal Cenotaphs of Jaipur
places.seoDescription: Gaitore, Jaipur: the marble and sandstone chhatris of the Kachhwaha rulers, used as the royal cremation ground from 1733, just off the Amber road.

images.alt: Carved marble chhatris at Gaitore
images.caption: Gaitore

overview.text: Just off the Jaipur–Amber road, Gaitore holds the cenotaphs (chhatris) of Jaipur's rulers. Jai Singh II chose it as the royal cremation ground, and from 1733 each Kachhwaha ruler was cremated here; the chhatris are carved from marble and sandstone. It is close to Jal Mahal on the same road.

places.name: Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing
places.summary: A museum of block-printed textiles in a restored haveli in Amer.
places.seoTitle: Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing, Amer (Jaipur)
places.seoDescription: Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing in Amer: block-printed textiles, tools and techniques in a UNESCO-awarded restored haveli near Amber Fort.

images.alt: The restored haveli housing the Anokhi Museum
images.caption: Anokhi Museum

overview.text: A ten-minute walk through the cobbled lanes of Amer, the Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing opened in 2005 in a restored haveli. It shows block-printed textiles alongside the tools and images that explain how they are made. The restoration won a UNESCO heritage conservation award in 2000.

items.body: Combine with Amber Fort and Panna Meena ka Kund.
See block printing at its source in Bagru, 32 km from Jaipur.

places.name: Johari Bazaar
places.summary: The old city's jewellery and textile street, beside Hawa Mahal.
places.seoTitle: Johari Bazaar & Jaipur's Markets: What to Buy
places.seoDescription: Shopping in Jaipur's old city: Johari Bazaar for jewellery and textiles, Bapu Bazaar for mojaris, Rajasthali for crafts — and Sunday closures.

images.alt: Shops along Johari Bazaar in Jaipur's old city
images.caption: Johari Bazaar

overview.text: Johari Bazaar is the old city's jewellery street, also known for clothes and textiles; it runs past Hawa Mahal. Bapu Bazaar is the place for mojari shoes and textiles, and Rajasthali, the Rajasthan Government showroom on MI Road, sells crafts at fixed prices; Nehru and Tripolia bazaars and the stalls at Badi and Choti Chaupar round out the old-city shopping.

items.body: Jewellery and gems in Johari Bazaar.
Lac bangles made by Jaipur artisans.
Block-printed Sanganeri, Bagru and Dabu textiles.
Most markets are closed on Sundays.
Rajasthali on MI Road is the government showroom if you prefer fixed prices.

how_to_reach.text: Johari Bazaar runs through the walled old city past Hawa Mahal. The metro's Pink Line ends at Badi Chaupar, at the bazaar's northern end.

places.name: Isarlat (Swarg Suli)
places.summary: A 60-ft victory tower near Tripolia Gate with views over the old city.
places.seoTitle: Isarlat (Swarg Suli) Jaipur: The Victory Tower
places.seoDescription: Isarlat, or Swarg Suli: a 60-ft minaret near Tripolia Gate in Jaipur's old city, built in 1749 by Raja Ishwari Singh, with views over the city.

overview.text: Isarlat, also called Swarg Suli ('heaven-piercing minaret'), is a 60-ft tower near Tripolia Gate in the old city. Raja Ishwari Singh built it in 1749 to mark a victory, and from the top there are wide views over Jaipur. It is a short walk from the City Palace and Jantar Mantar.

places.name: Sisodia Rani Garden
places.summary: A terraced Mughal-style garden 8 km from Jaipur on the Agra road.
places.seoTitle: Sisodia Rani Garden Jaipur: Terraces & Murals
places.seoDescription: Sisodia Rani Palace and Garden, 8 km from Jaipur on the Agra road: a terraced Mughal-style garden with fountains and murals of Radha and Krishna.

overview.text: Sisodia Rani Palace and Garden lies 8 km from Jaipur on the Agra road. Laid out in Mughal style over several terraces, it has fountains, water channels and pavilions painted with the legends of Radha and Krishna. Jai Singh II built it for his Sisodia queen. Nearby, the Vidyadhar garden is named after Jaipur's chief architect.

places.name: Jhalana Leopard Safari
places.summary: Safaris in a forest on Jaipur's edge, known for leopard sightings.
places.seoTitle: Jhalana Leopard Safari Jaipur: What to Expect
places.seoDescription: Jhalana, on Jaipur's south-eastern edge: a 1,978-hectare forest whose safaris are known for leopard sightings, minutes from the city.

images.alt: Leopards in the Jhalana forest, Jaipur
images.caption: Jhalana

overview.text: Jhalana is a 1,978-hectare forest block on Jaipur's south-eastern edge. Its safaris are known for leopard sightings — unusual this close to a big city. The dry deciduous forest is good for birdwatching, and inside are a royal hunting lodge (shikar oudhi) built in 1835 and a Kali temple.

places.name: Amber Fort Sound and Light Show
places.summary: The evening son-et-lumière at Amber Fort.
places.seoTitle: Amber Fort Sound & Light Show: Timings by Season
places.seoDescription: The Amber Fort sound and light show: Rajasthan Tourism's seasonal timings for the English and Hindi shows, and what the show covers.

overview.text: Every evening Amber Fort hosts a sound and light show that tells its history through local legends and folk music, with shows in English and Hindi. Show times change with the season, so check them with Rajasthan Tourism on the day. Amber is about 11 km from the city, so plan a cab or rickshaw back after the show.

places.name: Jaipur Kite Festival
places.summary: Kite flying over the city around 14 January (Makar Sankranti).
places.seoTitle: Jaipur Kite Festival: Makar Sankranti in the Pink City
places.seoDescription: Jaipur's Kite Festival around 14 January: kites fill the sky for Makar Sankranti, with a tourism-department festival and cultural shows.

overview.text: Around 14 January — Makar Sankranti — kites fill the sky over Jaipur. The tourism department holds a kite festival with cultural performances, and Galtaji draws its biggest crowds the same day. In the evening, fireworks and lit kites brighten the skyline.

places.name: Gangaur and Teej in Jaipur
places.summary: Jaipur's two great women's festivals, with royal processions.
places.seoTitle: Gangaur & Teej in Jaipur: Festival Dates & Processions
places.seoDescription: Gangaur (Chaitra, March–April) and Teej (monsoon) in Jaipur: what they celebrate and the procession through the City Palace.

overview.text: Gangaur, one of Rajasthan's most important festivals, honours Shiva and Parvati in the Hindu month of Chaitra (March–April). Gangaur begins the day after Holi and lasts 16 days, celebrating spring, harvest and marriage. Teej marks the monsoon; in Jaipur a grand procession carries an idol of Parvati through the City Palace.

places.name: Jaipur Literature Festival
places.summary: One of the world's biggest literary festivals, every January.
places.seoTitle: Jaipur Literature Festival (JLF): When & Where
places.seoDescription: The Jaipur Literature Festival: founded in 2006, held every January, and since 2025 at Hotel Clarks Amer.

overview.text: Founded in 2006 by Namita Gokhale and William Dalrymple, the Jaipur Literature Festival is held every January — the 2020 edition ran from 23 to 27 January at Diggi Palace. Since 2025 it has been held at Hotel Clarks Amer to make room for its crowds.

places.name: Bagru
places.summary: A block-printing village 32 km from Jaipur on the Ajmer road.
places.seoTitle: Bagru Block Printing Village near Jaipur
places.seoDescription: Bagru, 32 km southwest of Jaipur: the village of hand block printing with vegetable dyes and mud-resist Dabu prints — an easy half-day trip.

images.commons: File:Woman doing Block Printing at Bagru village, Jaipur, India.jpg
images.alt: A woman block-printing cloth at Bagru
images.caption: Bagru

overview.text:
Bagru lies about 32 km southwest of Jaipur on the Ajmer road. It is known for hand block printing with natural dyes, and especially for Dabu, a mud-resist technique in which a paste of mud is printed onto the cloth to keep the dye out.

Printers use wooden blocks and colour the cloth with vegetable dyes — indigo for blue, madder root for red, turmeric for yellow — giving Bagru prints their earthy tones and floral patterns.

items.body: Watch printers and dyers at work.
See the craft's history first at the Anokhi Museum in Amer.
Continue west to Sambhar Lake in winter for flamingos.

places.name: Chand Baori (Abhaneri)
places.summary: A vast 8th–9th-century stepwell in Abhaneri village.
places.seoTitle: Chand Baori Abhaneri: India's Great Stepwell
places.seoDescription: Chand Baori in Abhaneri: an 8th–9th-century stepwell with 3,500 steps over 13 storeys and the Harshat Mata temple beside it — a day trip from Jaipur.

images.alt: The geometric steps of Chand Baori stepwell
images.caption: Chand Baori

overview.text:
Chand Baori, in Abhaneri village, is a stepwell dated to the 8th–9th century. It has 3,500 narrow steps over 13 storeys; at the bottom the air is 5–6 °C cooler than at the surface.

Beside it stands the Harshat Mata temple.

places.name: Sambhar Lake
places.summary: India's largest inland salt lake, about 70 km from Jaipur — flamingos in winter.
places.seoTitle: Sambhar Salt Lake: Flamingos & Salt Pans near Jaipur
places.seoDescription: Sambhar, India's largest inland salt lake, about 70 km from Jaipur: winter flamingos, salt pans worked for a thousand years, and when to go.

images.alt: The salt flats of Sambhar Lake
images.caption: Sambhar Lake

overview.text: Sambhar is India's largest inland salt lake, about 70 km from Jaipur. Salt has been farmed in evaporation pans east of its dam for a thousand years. In winter the lake fills with flamingos and other migratory birds.

best_time.text: Come in winter for the flamingos; summer heat reaches 45 °C.

itineraries.title: Two days in Jaipur: the hill forts and the old city
itineraries.summary: Day one on the ridge of hill forts — Amber, Jaigarh and Nahargarh; day two on foot in the walled city at Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar, the City Palace and the bazaars.
itineraries.seoTitle: 2 Days in Jaipur Itinerary: Amber Fort to Hawa Mahal
itineraries.seoDescription: A realistic two-day Jaipur itinerary with timings, distances and 2026 ticket prices: Amber, Jaigarh and Nahargarh forts, then Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar and City Palace.

plan.overview: Jaipur's sights fall into two clusters, and this plan gives each its own day. Day 1 drives the ridge of hill forts north of the city — Amber, Jaigarh and Nahargarh — finishing with the view over Jaipur at dusk. Day 2 stays inside the walled old city, where Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar and the City Palace are a few minutes' walk apart, then the bazaars and an evening at Ram Niwas Garden. If one of your days is a Sunday, make it Day 1: most old-city bazaars close on Sundays.
plan.start: Jaipur (hotel in or near the walled city)
plan.season: October to March is most comfortable. April–June afternoons are extremely hot — start at 8–9 am and rest indoors after lunch. July–August brings most of the rain.
plan.difficulty: Easy to moderate — steep ramps at Amber and a lot of walking on Day 2
plan.transport: Day 1: taxi or app cab for the fort loop (about 35 km in total). Day 2: on foot in the old city, with an e-rickshaw or auto for the last leg.

days.title: Day 1 — Amber, Jaigarh and Nahargarh: the hill forts
days.summary: Amber's palaces in the cool of the morning, the cannon fort above it after lunch, and Nahargarh's ramparts for the late-afternoon view over the city.

stops.name: Jal Mahal (roadside view)
stops.note: Photo stop on the Amer road; the palace is seen from the promenade, not visited.

stops.name: Amber Fort
stops.note: Enter by Suraj Pol into Jaleb Chowk, then the Diwan-e-Aam and the Sheesh Mahal. Arriving at opening beats the tour-group crowds. Buy the two-day composite ticket here if you are using it.

stops.name: Lunch in Amer town
stops.note: Eat below the fort before driving up — there are few food options at Jaigarh.

stops.name: Jaigarh Fort
stops.note: The Jaivana cannon and views down onto Amber and Maota Lake. Jaigarh is run separately: pay at its gate, or use the City Palace Composite ticket.

stops.name: Nahargarh Fort
stops.note: Madhvendra Palace and the ramparts over Jaipur. Closing time varies by season and between sources — ask at the gate, and in winter (sunset around 5:30–5:45 pm) arrive by 4 pm.

days.travel: Old city → Amber about 11 km (20–45 minutes depending on traffic). Amber → Jaigarh about 2.5 km uphill. Jaigarh → Nahargarh along the ridge road, about 16 km from Amber in all. Nahargarh → old city about 6 km down Nahargarh Fort Road (20–25 minutes). Agree a fixed price for the whole loop with the driver before setting off.
days.driveTime: About 1.5–2 hours of driving across the day (estimate)
days.transport: Taxi or app cab for the day
days.meals: Breakfast before 8:30 am. Lunch in Amer town. Dinner back in the city — try dal baati churma or laal maas.
days.overnight: Jaipur — in or near the walled city, so Day 2 starts on foot
days.logistics: Carry water and a hat: the Amber ramps and Jaigarh ramparts have little shade. Monuments close on Dhulandi (the day after Holika Dahan).

days.title: Day 2 — The walled city: Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar and City Palace
days.summary: Three of Jaipur's best-known sights within a few minutes' walk, the bazaars in the afternoon, and street food beside the lit-up Albert Hall.

stops.name: Hawa Mahal
stops.note: See the 953-window facade from the street first, then enter from the rear and climb the ramps for the view over Siredeori Bazaar.

stops.name: Jantar Mantar
stops.note: A guide makes the instruments far easier to understand; the giant Vrihat Samrat Yantra sundial is the centrepiece.

stops.name: City Palace
stops.note: Enter at Gate 1 by Jantar Mantar. The Museum ticket covers the courtyards and galleries; the upper Chandra Mahal floors need the Royal Tour, sold only at the counter.

stops.name: Lunch and rest
stops.note: Get out of the midday sun before the markets.

stops.name: Johari Bazaar and Bapu Bazaar
stops.note: Jewellery and textiles on Johari; mojari shoes and block prints on Bapu. Most shops close on Sundays.

stops.name: Albert Hall (lit up) and Masala Chowk
stops.note: The museum building is lit in colour every evening; Masala Chowk in the same Ram Niwas Garden gathers Jaipur's street-food stalls.

days.travel: Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar and the City Palace are a short walk apart. Bapu Bazaar → Ram Niwas Garden is a short e-rickshaw or auto ride. The Metro Pink Line stops at Badi Chaupar beside Hawa Mahal.
days.meals: Lassi or kachori in the old city for breakfast; lunch near the City Palace; dinner at Masala Chowk.
days.overnight: Jaipur, or an evening train or flight onward
days.logistics: The old city's bazaars are busy and crowded; keep valuables close. Carry small cash for rickshaws, though UPI is widely accepted.

budget.assumptions: Per adult, monument entry and local transport only. Hotel, meals, guides and shopping are not included because they vary too widely to estimate honestly. Rates are those reported after the 1 January 2026 revision — confirm at the counter.

lines.label: Jaipur two-day composite ticket
lines.basis: Covers Amber, Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar, Nahargarh and Albert Hall; reported price, confirm on the day

lines.label: Or single tickets: Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar, Nahargarh
City Palace Composite (adds Jaigarh and Royal Cenotaphs)

booking.detail: Buy single or composite tickets at the Amber, Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar or Albert Hall counters; the composite is valid for two days.
Tickets at Gate 1 (near Jantar Mantar) or Gate 2 (Jaleb Chowk); the Chandra Mahal Royal Tour is sold only at the counter.
Book a cab for the Amber–Jaigarh–Nahargarh loop the evening before and fix the price and waiting time.
Book Jaipur–Delhi Shatabdi or Rajdhani services on IRCTC in advance, especially October–March.

alternatives: Indian visitors: the composite only saves money if you also go into Albert Hall — Amber, Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar and Nahargarh bought singly total ₹500.
Foreign visitors: the composite (about ₹1,700) is well below the four single tickets (₹2,800).
Planning to see both Jaigarh and the City Palace? Take the City Palace Composite (₹500) instead of the Museum ticket, and ask whether it can be used across two days.
Amber's evening sound and light show can replace the Nahargarh visit — check the season's show times.
On a Sunday, swap the bazaars for the Albert Hall Museum inside and a longer City Palace visit.
Families with young children: drop Jaigarh and keep a longer lunch break on Day 1.
tips: Be at Amber by 9 am: tour coaches arrive mid-morning.
Do the hill forts on the same day — they share one ridge road, so splitting them doubles the driving.
All state monuments and the City Palace close on Dhulandi, the day after Holika Dahan.
Hire licensed guides at the monument counters rather than from touts at the gates.

prep.title: Heat
prep.body: From April to June, keep outdoor sightseeing to the morning and late afternoon; carry water, a hat and sunscreen.

prep.title: Money
prep.body: UPI works at most counters and shops. International visitors can use the UPI One World wallet after a passport-and-visa check; carry some cash for rickshaws.

prep.title: Dress
prep.body: Shoulders and knees covered is respectful at temples such as Sila Devi inside Amber; comfortable shoes for the ramps and ramparts.

faqs.q: Is two days enough for Jaipur?
faqs.a: Two days covers the main sights — the three hill forts on one day and the walled city on the other. Add a third day for the Albert Hall Museum inside, Galtaji, or a slower pace.

faqs.q: Should I buy the Jaipur composite ticket?
faqs.a: Foreign visitors almost always save. Indian visitors save only if they also enter Albert Hall. Jaigarh and the City Palace are not part of it.

faqs.q: How do I get from Jaipur to Amber Fort?
faqs.a: It is about 11 km. An auto-rickshaw takes about 20–25 minutes and costs ₹200–250; a taxi for the full fort loop is easier if you are also going to Jaigarh and Nahargarh.

itineraries.title: Jaipur in one day: Amber, the old city and the lit-up museum
itineraries.summary: One full day for Jaipur's essentials: Amber Fort at opening, the Jal Mahal on the way back, then Hawa Mahal, City Palace and Jantar Mantar in the walled city, and the Albert Hall lit up at night.
itineraries.seoTitle: Jaipur 1-Day Itinerary: Amber Fort, City Palace & Hawa Mahal
itineraries.seoDescription: A realistic one-day Jaipur plan timed to real opening hours: Amber Fort at 9 am, Hawa Mahal, City Palace and Jantar Mantar, and the Albert Hall at night.

plan.overview: Jaipur's big sights are in two clusters: Amber on the hill road 11 km north, and the walled city around the City Palace. Start at Amber when it opens, before the heat and the coach groups. Back in the old city, see Hawa Mahal before it closes at 4:30 pm, then the City Palace and Jantar Mantar next door. The Albert Hall Museum reopens from 7 pm and is lit up at night.
plan.style: Fast-paced highlights day by car or rickshaw
plan.start: Your hotel in Jaipur (the airport is at Sanganer, about 10 km south of the centre)
plan.season: October to March is best: winter days of roughly 10–30°C. April–June is extremely hot; July–August brings most of the rain.

itineraries.title: Jaipur in four days, with Bagru and Sambhar
itineraries.summary: Four days in and around Jaipur: the walled city, the three hill forts on the ridge, a day out to Bagru's block printers and Sambhar salt lake, and Galtaji's temples and the bazaars to finish.
itineraries.seoTitle: Jaipur 4-Day Itinerary with Bagru and Sambhar Lake
itineraries.seoDescription: Four days in Jaipur at an easy pace: the walled city, Amber, Jaigarh and Nahargarh, a day trip to Bagru block printers and Sambhar salt lake, then Galtaji.

plan.overview: Four days let you see Jaipur without rushing and get out of the city once. Day 1 is the walled city on foot and by rickshaw. Day 2 follows the ridge road from Amber up to Jaigarh and along to Nahargarh for the view at dusk. Day 3 heads south-west to Bagru, where cloth is still hand block-printed with natural dyes, and on to Sambhar, India's largest inland salt lake, with flamingos in winter. Day 4 is the Galtaji temple complex in the eastern hills and a last round of the bazaars.
plan.style: Unhurried city stay with one rural day trip
plan.end: Jaipur (the airport is about 10 km south of the centre)
plan.season: October to March is best; Sambhar's flamingos and migratory birds come in winter. Summer reaches the mid-40s °C, and Sambhar's salt pans touch 45°C.
plan.transport: Car with driver for Days 2 and 3; rickshaws or app taxis in the old city.

budget.assumptions: Per adult, entry fees only. The two-day state composite ticket covers Amber, Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar, Nahargarh and Albert Hall; the City Palace Composite ticket adds Jaigarh.

Ask your hotel to arrange a hands-on session with a Bagru printing family in advance.

alternatives: Prefer architecture to salt flats? Swap Day 3 for Abhaneri's Chand Baori stepwell, about 95 km (2 hours) away.
Want wildlife? Add a morning leopard safari in Jhalana on Jaipur's south-eastern edge.
tips: Buy the City Palace Composite ticket on Day 1 — it also covers Jaigarh on Day 2.
Hawa Mahal closes at 4:30 pm; go before the City Palace if you're late.
Start Day 3 early: Sambhar is about 70 km from Jaipur and has little shade.

prep.title: Sambhar

prep.title: Galtaji

faqs.a: In winter, when the lake fills with flamingos and migratory birds.

itineraries.title: Three days in Jaipur: old city, Amer and the quieter sights
itineraries.summary: Day one in the walled city, day two at Amer with its stepwell, block-print museum and hill forts, and day three at the royal cenotaphs, Galtaji and the Mughal gardens on the Agra road.
itineraries.seoTitle: 3 Days in Jaipur Itinerary: Old City, Amer & Galtaji
itineraries.seoDescription: A realistic 3-day Jaipur plan with timings and 2026 tickets: City Palace and Hawa Mahal, Amber, Panna Meena ka Kund and Nahargarh, then Gaitore, Galtaji and Birla Mandir.

plan.overview: Three days lets you see Jaipur's three clusters without rushing. Day 1 is the walled city, all on foot. Day 2 is Amer — the fort, the old village with its stepwell and block-print museum, then the ridge forts. Day 3 covers the quieter sights most two-day visitors miss: the royal cenotaphs at Gaitore, Galtaji's temple gorge and the Mughal-style gardens on the Agra road. Days 1 and 2 fall within the two-day validity of the state composite ticket.
plan.style: Heritage city break with crafts and food, easy pace
plan.start: Jaipur (hotel in or near the walled city)
plan.season: October to March is most comfortable. April–June afternoons are extremely hot; start early and rest after lunch. The Anokhi Museum closes for maintenance from about mid-May to 15 July.
plan.difficulty: Easy to moderate — ramps at Amber, steep paths at Galtaji
plan.transport: Day 1 on foot and e-rickshaw; Days 2–3 by taxi or app cab.

days.title: Day 1 — The walled city
days.summary: Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar and the City Palace a few minutes apart, the bazaars in the afternoon, and Albert Hall lit up at night.

stops.name: Hawa Mahal
stops.note: See the 953-window facade from the street, then enter from the rear. Buy the two-day composite ticket here.

stops.name: Jantar Mantar
stops.note: Hire a guide to understand the instruments, including the 27 m sundial.

stops.name: City Palace
stops.note: Take the Composite ticket (₹500) if you also want Jaigarh tomorrow and the Royal Cenotaphs on Day 3 — ask at the counter how long it is valid.

stops.name: Johari Bazaar and Bapu Bazaar
stops.note: Jewellery, textiles and mojari shoes; most shops close on Sundays.

stops.name: Albert Hall and Masala Chowk
stops.note: The building is lit in colour every evening; Masala Chowk in Ram Niwas Garden gathers Jaipur's street food.

days.travel: The three main sights are a short walk apart; e-rickshaw to Ram Niwas Garden in the evening.
days.meals: Lunch near the City Palace; dinner at Masala Chowk.

days.title: Day 3 — Gaitore, Galtaji and the Agra-road gardens
days.summary: The quiet royal cenotaphs, the temple gorge at Galtaji, a terraced Mughal-style garden, and sunset at Birla Mandir.

stops.name: Gaitore (royal cenotaphs)
stops.note: Marble and sandstone chhatris of Jaipur's rulers, just off the Amer road; rarely crowded.

stops.name: Galtaji
stops.note: Temples and water tanks in a gorge about 10 km east of the city, fed by the Gaumukh spring. Steep in places; the resident monkeys snatch food.

stops.name: Sisodia Rani Garden
stops.note: Terraced garden with fountains and Radha–Krishna murals, about 8 km out on the Agra road.

stops.name: Birla Mandir
stops.note: White-marble Lakshmi Narayan temple below Moti Dungri; lovely at dusk.

days.travel: Gaitore is on the Amer road; Galtaji and Sisodia Rani Garden lie east on the Agra road; Birla Mandir is back in the city — about 40 km in total (estimate).

days.overnight: Jaipur, or an evening train or flight onward

Tickets at Gate 1 (near Jantar Mantar) or Gate 2 (Jaleb Chowk); ask whether the Composite can be used across days.
Book a car for Days 2 and 3 with a fixed price and waiting time.

alternatives: Craft lovers: replace Galtaji and the garden on Day 3 with Bagru, about 32 km out on the Ajmer road, for hand block printing with natural dyes.
Families: on Day 3, swap Galtaji for a Jhalana leopard safari (book ahead) and keep the gardens.
Evening option on Day 2: the Amber sound and light show instead of Nahargarh.
On a Sunday, do Day 2 or Day 3 first — the bazaars are mostly closed.
tips: Be at Amber by 9 am, before the tour coaches.
Keep food out of sight at Galtaji — the monkeys are bold.
Most monuments close on Dhulandi, the day after Holika Dahan.

prep.title: Heat
prep.body: April to June: keep outdoor sightseeing to the morning and late afternoon, and carry water.

prep.title: Money
prep.body: UPI works widely; international visitors can use UPI One World after a passport check. Carry small cash for rickshaws and temple shoe stands.

prep.title: Dress
prep.body: Cover shoulders and knees at Galtaji, Birla Mandir and the temples inside Amber.

faqs.q: Is three days too long for Jaipur?
faqs.a: No — two days covers the headline sights, and the third lets you add Amer village, Gaitore and Galtaji at an easy pace.

faqs.q: Which composite ticket should I buy?
faqs.a: The state two-day composite covers Amber, Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar, Nahargarh and Albert Hall. The City Palace sells its own; its Composite adds Jaigarh and the Royal Cenotaphs.

faqs.q: When is the Anokhi Museum closed?
faqs.a: Every Monday, and for gallery maintenance from about mid-May to 15 July.

guides.title: Jaipur festivals through the year
guides.summary: When to time your trip for kites, books, Gangaur and Teej.
guides.seoTitle: Jaipur Festivals Calendar: Kites, JLF, Gangaur, Teej
guides.seoDescription: When Jaipur celebrates: the Kite Festival around 14 January, the Literature Festival in January, Gangaur in March–April, Teej in the monsoon and Rajasthan Day.

body.intro: Jaipur's festivals are as good a reason to visit as its forts. Here is when they fall and what to expect.

sections.heading: January: kites and books
sections.text: Around 14 January (Makar Sankranti) kites fill the sky and the tourism department holds a kite festival; Galtaji is busiest that day. The Jaipur Literature Festival is also held in January, since 2025 at Hotel Clarks Amer.

sections.heading: March–April: Gangaur
sections.text: Gangaur, one of Rajasthan's most important festivals, honours Shiva and Parvati in the month of Chaitra.

sections.heading: Monsoon: Teej
sections.text: Teej celebrates the monsoon; in Jaipur a procession carries an idol of Parvati through the City Palace.

sections.heading: Krishna festivals
sections.text: Janmashtami and Holi bring thousands of devotees to the Govind Dev Ji temple.

sections.heading: Rajasthan Day
sections.text: The state's foundation day is marked by a three-day Rajasthan Festival organised by the tourism department.

guides.summary: Rajasthani dishes, street food, bazaars and crafts.
guides.seoTitle: Jaipur Food & Shopping Guide: Dishes, Bazaars, Crafts
guides.seoDescription: What to eat and buy in Jaipur: dal baati churma and street food at Masala Chowk, Johari and Bapu bazaars, lac bangles and Bagru block prints.

body.intro: Jaipur is as much about eating and shopping as about palaces. Here is where to start.

sections.heading: Dishes to try
sections.text: Dal baati churma, kachori, mirchi bada, ker sangri and, for meat-eaters, laal maas.

sections.heading: Street food in one place
sections.text: Masala Chowk in Ram Niwas Bagh gathers Jaipur's street-food stalls together — easy to combine with the Albert Hall Museum.

sections.heading: Where to shop
sections.text: Johari Bazaar for jewellery and textiles, Bapu Bazaar for mojari shoes, and Rajasthali — the government showroom on MI Road — for fixed-price crafts. Most markets close on Sundays.

sections.heading: What to buy
sections.text: Block-printed Sanganeri, Bagru and Dabu textiles, lac bangles and gemstones.

sections.heading: See the craft
sections.text: The Anokhi Museum in Amer explains block printing; in Bagru, 32 km away, you can watch printers using vegetable dyes.

checklist: Cash and UPI for small shops

guides.summary: Airport, trains, the metro, and distances to the sights.
guides.seoTitle: Getting Around Jaipur: Airport, Metro & Distances
guides.seoDescription: Reaching and getting around Jaipur: Sanganer airport, trains from Delhi and Agra, the Pink Line metro, and distances to Amber, Jaigarh, Galtaji and day trips.

body.intro: Jaipur is easy to reach and compact at its core; the forts and day trips need a car or rickshaw.

sections.heading: Arriving
sections.text: Jaipur International Airport is at Sanganer, about 10 km south of the centre. Jaipur is about 268 km from Delhi and 232 km from Agra by road, and has direct trains — including the Shatabdi and Rajdhani — to Delhi and other major cities.

sections.heading: In the city
sections.text: The Pink Line metro runs east–west between Mansarovar and Badi Chaupar in the old city. Hawa Mahal, the City Palace and Jantar Mantar are a short walk apart.

sections.heading: To the forts
sections.text: Amber is about 11 km away — about 20–25 minutes and 200–250 rupees by rickshaw, says Incredible India. Jaigarh is about 15 km away, above Amber. Nahargarh's steps can be climbed for free.

sections.heading: Short hops
sections.text: Galtaji is about 10 km east; Sisodia Rani Garden 8 km out on the Agra road; Moti Dungri about 6 km from Jaipur Junction.

sections.heading: Day trips
sections.text: Bagru is about 32 km southwest on the Ajmer road; Sambhar Lake about 70 km away. Hire a car for these.

guides.title: First time in Jaipur: mistakes to avoid
guides.summary: Opening hours, Sundays, heat, tickets and paperwork.
guides.seoTitle: First Time in Jaipur: Mistakes to Avoid
guides.seoDescription: Avoid the common first-timer mistakes in Jaipur: Hawa Mahal closing at 4:30, Sunday bazaars, summer heat, City Palace tickets, Jal Mahal access and e-visa timing.

body.intro: Most of Jaipur's frustrations are about timing. These are the ones that catch first-time visitors.

sections.heading: Leaving Hawa Mahal too late
sections.text: It closes at 4:30 pm, and the entrance is at the back, not on the famous façade.

sections.heading: Expecting to enter Jal Mahal
sections.text: The Water Palace is not open to tourists; you see it from the promenade — or from Nahargarh above.

sections.heading: Shopping on a Sunday
sections.text: Most bazaars are closed on Sundays.

sections.heading: The wrong City Palace ticket
sections.text: The standard ticket covers only the first floor of the Chandra Mahal; the upper rooms need the Royal Splendour ticket.

sections.heading: Underestimating the heat
sections.text: Summers are long and extremely hot; plan sights for mornings and evenings.

sections.heading: Paperwork and payments
sections.text: Apply for an e-Tourist visa at least 4 days ahead. Foreign visitors can pay by UPI with the UPI One World wallet. The tourist infoline is 1800-11-1363; 112 is the emergency number.
